title: Customization and the Rewards Benefit
lessons: The player first engages with Starbucks through the unusually customizable drink order itself.
The player is already in Starbucks Rewards and sees a monthly benefit that covers one drink customization up to the program limit.

text: The player first engages with Starbucks through the unusually customizable drink order itself.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: At what point does my order become embarrassing?

entry-first-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Around the third modifier, but I will still make it.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: You encourage this.

entry-first-4.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Milk, syrup, foam, temperature, shots, toppings. Customization is part of the product, not a secret menu accident.

choice-first.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: What do you make of that?

choices.text: I like being able to get exactly what I want.
Too many options makes ordering feel like work.
I would rather have a coffee shop tell me what it makes well.

first-1.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Then customization is part of the comfort for you.

first-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Then keep it simple. Customization is an option, not a citizenship test.

first-2-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Tall coffee.

first-2-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Beautifully legible.

first-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: That is a different kind of coffee relationship, and I get the appeal.
The player is already in Starbucks Rewards and sees a monthly benefit that covers one drink customization up to the program limit.

entry-return-1.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: One customization is on me this month.

entry-return-2.speaker: PLAYER
text: You mean the thing I already pay extra for?

entry-return-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Within the Mod Monday program limit, yes.

entry-return-4.speaker: PLAYER
text: So my existing habit became a loyalty perk.

entry-return-5.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: I know what you like. I might as well reward the expensive part.

choice-return.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: What do you make of that?

choices.text: I was going to add it anyway, so that is useful.
A free modification is tiny compared with what I spend here.
I do not want a reward system nudging me to decorate every drink.

return-1.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: That is exactly when a small perk feels real.

return-2.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: It is a small benefit. I am not going to call two dollars life-changing.

return-3.speaker: STARBUCKS
text: Then order it plain. A reward does not need to invent a need.
